requirement: Unevaluated operand remains distinguishable from false operand

obligations.note: creating the lambda object always happens, regardless of whether it's later called
left is true, so AND must evaluate the right operand -- mark.call() actually runs

THE case this fixture exists for: left is false, so AND short-circuits and mark.call() is NEVER invoked -- not 'called and returned false', genuinely never entered. Ground truth confirmed via an observable side channel (the log array), not inferred from the boolean result alone: 'false and X' returns false whether or not X ran, so the return value cannot itself prove this.
left is false, so OR must evaluate the right operand

left is true, so OR short-circuits and mark.call() is NEVER invoked. The result (true) would be identical if this line ran and returned false -- the log array is what actually proves the short-circuit, not the return value.

notes: Uses an explicit log array (mutated by a captured lambda) as an observable side channel for whether the right operand was actually evaluated, rather than relying on the boolean return value -- the return value alone is provably insufficient here: 'run_and(false, true)' and a hypothetical buggy non-short-circuiting AND both return false, and 'run_or(true, false)' and a hypothetical buggy non-short-circuiting OR both return true. All four inputs' log contents confirmed directly via pilot/fixtures/driver.gd on the pinned Godot 4.7.1 engine -- this is a verified ground truth about short-circuit evaluation, not an assumption from language documentation. The right operand's own lambda body (lines 5-6, 12-13) provides a clean, ordinary statement-obligation signal for 'was it evaluated' -- no branch-evidence schema extension needed here, unlike F029's same-line ternary case, since the lambda body lines are genuinely separate physical lines. Removed on 2026-09-19: obligations on lines 3 and 10 (the run_and/run_or func signatures), which predated the F032/F034 convention that function signature lines are never statement obligations -- found by a corpus-wide lint pass while building the lifecycle domain. Their removal changes no other fact in this oracle; both were always expected_hit=true in every input.
